claim: TMEM120A has a pivotal function in adipocyte differentiation and metabolism.
source: TMEM120A, a member of the transmembrane protein 120 (TMEM120) family, has a pivotal function in adipocyte differentiation and metabolism
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research on TMEM120A's role in adipocyte biology.

claim: TMEM120A may contribute to sensing mechanical pain by functioning as an ion channel named TACAN.
source: TMEM120A, a member of the transmembrane protein 120 (TMEM120) family, has a pivotal function in adipocyte differentiation and metabolism, and may also contribute to sensing mechanical pain by functioning as an ion channel named TACAN.
evidence: This claim references prior literature suggesting TMEM120A functions as a mechanosensitive ion channel.

claim: Expression of TMEM120A is not sufficient in mediating poking-induced currents in cells.
source: Here we report that expression of TMEM120A is not sufficient in mediating poking- or stretch-induced currents in cells
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from whole-cell patch-clamp recordings shown in Figure 1.

claim: Expression of TMEM120A is not sufficient in mediating stretch-induced currents in cells.
source: Here we report that expression of TMEM120A is not sufficient in mediating poking- or stretch-induced currents in cells
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from cell-attached and inside-out patch-clamp recordings shown in Figure 1.

claim: The cryo-EM structure of HsTMEM120A in complex with CoASH has been solved.
source: have solved cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of human TMEM120A (HsTMEM120A) in complex with an endogenous metabolic cofactor (coenzyme A, CoASH) and in the apo form.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data presented in Figures 2-4 and deposited in PDB (7F3T).

claim: The cryo-EM structure of HsTMEM120A in the apo form has been solved.
source: have solved cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of human TMEM120A (HsTMEM120A) in complex with an endogenous metabolic cofactor (coenzyme A, CoASH) and in the apo form.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data presented in Figure 5 and deposited in PDB (7F3U).

claim: HsTMEM120A forms a symmetrical homodimer.
source: HsTMEM120A forms a symmetrical homodimer with each monomer containing an amino-terminal coiled-coil motif followed by a transmembrane domain with six membrane-spanning helices.
evidence: This claim is supported by cryo-EM structural data shown in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: Each monomer of HsTMEM120A contains an amino-terminal coiled-coil motif.
source: HsTMEM120A forms a symmetrical homodimer with each monomer containing an amino-terminal coiled-coil motif followed by a transmembrane domain with six membrane-spanning helices.
evidence: This claim is supported by cryo-EM structural data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Each monomer of HsTMEM120A contains a transmembrane domain with six membrane-spanning helices.
source: HsTMEM120A forms a symmetrical homodimer with each monomer containing an amino-terminal coiled-coil motif followed by a transmembrane domain with six membrane-spanning helices.
evidence: This claim is supported by cryo-EM structural data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: A CoASH molecule is hosted in a deep cavity within the transmembrane domain of HsTMEM120A.
source: Within the transmembrane domain, a CoASH molecule is hosted in a deep cavity and forms specific interactions with nearby amino acid residues.
evidence: This claim is supported by cryo-EM density maps and structural models shown in Figures 4B, 4E-G.

claim: CoASH forms specific interactions with nearby amino acid residues in HsTMEM120A.
source: Within the transmembrane domain, a CoASH molecule is hosted in a deep cavity and forms specific interactions with nearby amino acid residues.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data showing hydrogen bonds, salt bridges, and π-π interactions in Figures 4E-G.

claim: Mutation of Trp193 to Ala dramatically reduced the binding affinity of HsTMEM120A with CoASH.
source: Mutation of a central tryptophan residue involved in binding CoASH dramatically reduced the binding affinity of HsTMEM120A with CoASH.
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC data comparing wild-type and W193A mutant shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: HsTMEM120A exhibits distinct conformations at the states with or without CoASH bound.
source: HsTMEM120A exhibits distinct conformations at the states with or without CoASH bound.
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of cryo-EM structures shown in Figure 5C-E.

claim: TMEM120A may have alternative functional roles potentially involved in CoASH transport, sensing, or metabolism.
source: Our results suggest that TMEM120A may have alternative functional roles potentially involved in CoASH transport, sensing, or metabolism.
evidence: This claim is speculative, based on the structural finding of CoASH binding and the lack of mechanosensitive channel activity.

claim: Mechanosensation converts mechanical forces into electrochemical signals during various physiological processes.
source: Through a fundamental cellular process known as mechanosensation, mechanical forces are converted into electrochemical signals during various physiological processes, such as touch, hearing, pain sensation, osmoregulation, and cell volume regulation (Garcia-Anoveros and Corey, 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to established literature on mechanosensation.

claim: Various types of ion channels involved in sensing and transducing mechanical force signals have been identified.
source: In the past decades, various types of ion channels involved in sensing and transducing mechanical force signals have been identified (Jin et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a review article.

claim: MscL and MscS serve as emergency release valves on the membrane by sensing and responding to membrane tension.
source: Among them, mechanosensitive channels of large and small conductances (MscL and MscS) serve as emergency release valves on the membrane by sensing and responding to membrane tension (Booth and Blount, 2012; Haswell et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research on MscL and MscS channels.

claim: Members of the MscL family are present in bacteria, archaea, or fungi.
source: While members of the MscL family are present in bacteria, archaea, or fungi, and those of the MscS family exist in plants or microbes, they are not found in animals (Booth et al., 2007; Pivetti et al., 2003; Wilson et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research on the phylogenetic distribution of MscL.

claim: Members of the MscS family exist in plants or microbes.
source: While members of the MscL family are present in bacteria, archaea, or fungi, and those of the MscS family exist in plants or microbes, they are not found in animals (Booth et al., 2007; Pivetti et al., 2003; Wilson et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research on the phylogenetic distribution of MscS.

claim: MscL and MscS are not found in animals.
source: While members of the MscL family are present in bacteria, archaea, or fungi, and those of the MscS family exist in plants or microbes, they are not found in animals (Booth et al., 2007; Pivetti et al., 2003; Wilson et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research on the phylogenetic distribution of mechanosensitive channels.

claim: Piezo channels are involved in cellular mechanosensation processes crucial for touch perception, proprioception, red blood cell volume regulation, and other physiological functions in animals and plants.
source: Piezo channels are involved in cellular mechanosensation processes crucial for touch perception, proprioception, red blood cell volume regulation, and other physiological functions in animals and plants (Mousavi et al., 2021; Murthy et al., 2017; Radin et al., 2021; Xiao, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research on Piezo channels.

claim: TMEM120 is a family of membrane proteins widespread in animals and plants.
source: Transmembrane protein 120 (TMEM120) is a family of membrane proteins wide spread in animals and plants, and was originally identified as a nuclear envelope protein through a proteomic approach (Malik et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research identifying TMEM120.

claim: TMEM120 was originally identified as a nuclear envelope protein through a proteomic approach.
source: Transmembrane protein 120 (TMEM120) is a family of membrane proteins wide spread in animals and plants, and was originally identified as a nuclear envelope protein through a proteomic approach (Malik et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the original proteomic study.

claim: Two paralogs of TMEM120 (TMEM120A and TMEM120B) exist in mammals.
source: Two paralogs of TMEM120 (TMEM120A and TMEM120B) exist in mammals, and they have crucial functional roles in adipocyte differentiation and metabolism (Batrakou et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research on TMEM120 paralogs.

claim: TMEM120A and TMEM120B have crucial functional roles in adipocyte differentiation and metabolism.
source: Two paralogs of TMEM120 (TMEM120A and TMEM120B) exist in mammals, and they have crucial functional roles in adipocyte differentiation and metabolism (Batrakou et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research on TMEM120 function.

claim: Knockout of Tmem120a in mice led to a lipodystrophy syndrome with insulin resistance and metabolic defects when the animals were exposed to a high-fat diet.
source: Knockout of Tmem120a in mice led to a lipodystrophy syndrome with insulin resistance and metabolic defects when the animals were exposed to a high-fat diet (Czapiewski et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a prior mouse knockout study.

claim: TMEM120A has been reported to function as an ion channel involved in sensing mechanical pain and thereby termed TACAN.
source: Recently, TMEM120A has been reported to function as an ion channel involved in sensing mechanical pain and thereby termed TACAN (Beaulieu-Laroche et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the original TACAN paper.

claim: TMEM120A is expressed in a subset of nociceptors.
source: The protein is expressed in a subset of nociceptors and is associated with mechanically evoked currents in heterologous cell lines.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research on TMEM120A expression.

claim: TMEM120A is associated with mechanically evoked currents in heterologous cell lines.
source: The protein is expressed in a subset of nociceptors and is associated with mechanically evoked currents in heterologous cell lines.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research on TMEM120A function.

claim: TACAN protein exhibited nonselective cation channel activity when heterologously expressed in cell lines or reconstituted in liposomes.
source: Besides, TACAN protein exhibited nonselective cation channel activity when heterologously expressed in cell lines or reconstituted in liposomes (Beaulieu-Laroche et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research on TACAN channel activity.

claim: Heterologously expressed TMEM120A only mediated a picoampere-level of increase of stretch-induced currents on top of the endogenous currents.
source: In the previous report (Beaulieu-Laroche et al., 2020), heterologously expressed TMEM120A only mediated a picoampere-level of increase of stretch-induced currents on top of the endogenous currents and failed to respond to poking stimulation.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the prior TACAN paper.

claim: Heterologously expressed TMEM120A failed to respond to poking stimulation.
source: In the previous report (Beaulieu-Laroche et al., 2020), heterologously expressed TMEM120A only mediated a picoampere-level of increase of stretch-induced currents on top of the endogenous currents and failed to respond to poking stimulation.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the prior TACAN paper.

claim: TMEM120A appeared to be more efficiently activated via a pillar-based mechanical simulation at the cell-substrate interface.
source: However, it appeared to be more efficiently activated via a pillar-based mechanical simulation at the cell-substrate interface.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the prior TACAN paper.

claim: The single-channel conductance of the TMEM120A-mediated currents measured in cells was 11.5 pS.
source: The single-channel conductance of the TMEM120A-mediated currents measured in cells was 11.5 pS.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the prior TACAN paper.

claim: Reconstituted TMEM120A proteins were shown to mediate spontaneous channel activities with an estimated single-channel conductance of ~250 pS.
source: Surprisingly, reconstituted TMEM120A proteins were shown to mediate spontaneous channel activities with an estimated single-channel conductance of ~250 pS (Beaulieu-Laroche et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the prior TACAN paper.

claim: When purified HsTMEM120A protein was reconstituted into GUVs, pressure-dependent channel activities were rarely observed during the single-channel recording processes.
source: Under our experimental conditions, when the purified HsTMEM120A protein was reconstituted into GUVs, pressure-dependent channel activities were rarely observed during the single-channel recording processes.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from single-channel recordings shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Out of over 200 patches measured from HsTMEM120A-reconstituted GUVs, only two exhibited pressure-dependent mini-conductance channel activities.
source: As shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1, out of over 200 (ie, 217) patches measured, only two exhibited pressure-dependent mini-conductance channel activities.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from single-channel recordings shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: TMEM120 protein shares structural similarities with ELOVL protein.
source: Recently, it has been reported that TMEM120 protein shares structural similarities with a membrane-embedded enzyme named elongation of very long chain fatty acid (ELOVL) protein (Niu et al., 2021; Xue et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to recent structural studies.

claim: ELOVLs catalyze a condensation reaction between acyl-coA and malonyl-CoA to produce 3-keto acyl-CoA and release CoASH as well as CO2 as byproducts.
source: ELOVLs catalyze a condensation reaction between acyl-coA and malonyl-CoA to produce 3-keto acyl-CoA and release CoASH as well as CO2 as byproducts (Nie et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research on ELOVL enzymatic activity.

claim: TMEM120A did not exhibit ELOVL-like enzymatic activity when malonyl-CoA and stearoyl-CoA were supplied as substrates.
source: Although TMEM120A did not exhibit ELOVL-like enzymatic activity when malonyl-CoA and stearoyl-CoA were supplied as substrates (Niu et al., 2021), it is possible that TMEM120A may utilize different substrates or catalyze a reaction distinct from that of ELOVLs if it functions as an enzyme.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a prior study testing TMEM120A enzymatic activity.

claim: In C. elegans, the function of TMEM120 is related to incorporation of fatty acids into triacylglycerol.
source: In C. elegans, the function of TMEM120 is related to incorporation of fatty acids into triacylglycerol, and deficiency of TMEM120 in C. elegans is associated with a reduction of triacylglycerol level and lipid droplet size (Li et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a prior study on C. elegans TMEM120.

claim: Deficiency of TMEM120 in C. elegans is associated with a reduction of triacylglycerol level and lipid droplet size.
source: In C. elegans, the function of TMEM120 is related to incorporation of fatty acids into triacylglycerol, and deficiency of TMEM120 in C. elegans is associated with a reduction of triacylglycerol level and lipid droplet size (Li et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a prior study on C. elegans TMEM120.

claim: Co-expression of TMEM120A with Piezo2 reduced mechanically activated currents.
source: Co-expression of TMEM120A with Piezo2 reduced mechanically activated currents, and it was suggested that TMEM120A may function as a negative modulator of Piezo2 channel activity by modifying the lipid content of the cell (Del Rosario et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a prior study on TMEM120A-Piezo2 interaction.

claim: TMEM120A may function as a negative modulator of Piezo2 channel activity by modifying the lipid content of the cell.
source: Co-expression of TMEM120A with Piezo2 reduced mechanically activated currents, and it was suggested that TMEM120A may function as a negative modulator of Piezo2 channel activity by modifying the lipid content of the cell (Del Rosario et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a prior study on TMEM120A-Piezo2 interaction.

claim: The two monomers of HsTMEM120A proteins are related by a twofold symmetry axis running through their interface and perpendicular to the membrane plane.
source: The two monomers of HsTMEM120A proteins are related by a twofold symmetry axis running through their interface and perpendicular to the membrane plane.
evidence: This claim is supported by cryo-EM structural data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Each monomer of HsTMEM120A contains an N-terminal soluble domain (NTD) on the cytosolic side.
source: Each monomer contains an N-terminal soluble domain (NTD) on the cytosolic side and a transmembrane domain (TMD) embedded in a lipid bilayer (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by cryo-EM structural data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Each monomer of HsTMEM120A contains a transmembrane domain (TMD) embedded in a lipid bilayer.
source: Each monomer contains an N-terminal soluble domain (NTD) on the cytosolic side and a transmembrane domain (TMD) embedded in a lipid bilayer (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by cryo-EM structural data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: There are two α-helices (IH1 and IH2) in the NTD of each HsTMEM120A monomer.
source: There are two α-helices (intracellular helices 1 and 2, IH1 and IH2) in the NTD of each monomer (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by cryo-EM structural data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: IH1, IH2, and their symmetry-related ones in the adjacent monomer collectively form a coiled-coil structure.
source: IH1, IH2, and their symmetry-related ones in the adjacent monomer collectively form a coiled-coil structure with the long axis running approximately parallel to the membrane plane (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by cryo-EM structural data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The TMD of HsTMEM120A contains a bundle of six transmembrane helices (TM1-6) forming an asymmetric funnel with a wide opening on the intracellular side and a bottleneck on the extracellular side.
source: The TMD contains a bundle of six transmembrane helices (TM1-6) forming an asymmetric funnel with a wide opening on the intracellular side and a bottleneck on the extracellular side (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by cryo-EM structural data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Between NTD and TMD, there is a hinge-like motif (HM) with two long loops and a short amphipathic α-helix positioned near the membrane surface on the intracellular side.
source: Between NTD and TMD, there is a hinge-like motif (HM) with two long loops and a short amphipathic α-helix positioned near the membrane surface on the intracellular side.
evidence: This claim is supported by cryo-EM structural data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The HM intercalates at the gap between the TMDs of two adjacent monomers and serves to stabilize the dimer by interacting with both subunits.
source: The HM intercalates at the gap between the TMDs of two adjacent monomers and serves to stabilize the dimer by interacting with both subunits (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by cryo-EM structural data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The HsTMEM120A protein reconstituted in nanodiscs contains a CoASH molecule per monomer that is from an endogenous cellular source and copurified along with the protein.
source: Unexpectedly, the HsTMEM120A protein reconstituted in nanodiscs contains a CoASH molecule per monomer that is from an endogenous cellular source and copurified along with the protein (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by cryo-EM density, mass spectrometry, and ITC data shown in Figures 4B-D.

claim: A small-molecule density is observed in the intracellular funnel-like cavity of each HsTMEM120A monomer and the density matches well with the CoASH model.
source: Firstly, a small-molecule density is observed in the intracellular funnel-like cavity of each monomer and the density matches well with the CoASH model (Figure 4B) but not with the CoA derivatives (such as acetyl-CoA or fatty acyl CoA) or other nucleotide analogs (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by cryo-EM density maps shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mass spectrometry analysis on the perchloric acid extract of the purified HsTMEM120A protein indicates that the protein does contain CoASH.
source: Secondly, mass spectrometry (MS) analysis on the perchloric acid extract of the purified HsTMEM120A protein indicates that the protein does contain CoASH (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The CoASH molecule can bind to the ligand-free HsTMEM120A protein with a dissociation constant (Kd) of 0.69 ± 0.05 μM.
source: Thirdly, the CoASH molecule can bind to the ligand-free HsTMEM120A protein with a dissociation constant (Kd) of 0.69 ± 0.05 μM (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The CoASH molecule assumes a bent conformation in the HsTMEM120A binding site.
source: As shown in Figure 4B, the CoASH molecule assumes a bent conformation and forms numerous specific interactions with amino acid residues on the lumen surface of the cavity (Figure 4E–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by cryo-EM structural data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The amino acid residues involved in binding CoASH are highly conserved among various TMEM120A and TMEM120B homologs from different species.
source: The amino acid residues involved in binding CoASH are highly conserved among various TMEM120A and TMEM120B homologs from different species (Figure 4—figure supplements 2 and 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 4—figure supplements 2 and 3.

claim: The 5-pyrophosphate and 3-phosphate groups of CoASH are positioned at the entrance of the cavity.
source: The 5-pyrophosphate and 3-phosphate groups of CoASH are positioned at the entrance of the cavity, while the adenosine and cysteamine groups of CoASH are inserted deep in the intracellular cavity pocket of HsTMEM120A in a key-lock mode (Figure 4B,E–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by cryo-EM structural data shown in Figures 4B, E-G.

claim: The adenosine and cysteamine groups of CoASH are inserted deep in the intracellular cavity pocket of HsTMEM120A in a key-lock mode.
source: The 5-pyrophosphate and 3-phosphate groups of CoASH are positioned at the entrance of the cavity, while the adenosine and cysteamine groups of CoASH are inserted deep in the intracellular cavity pocket of HsTMEM120A in a key-lock mode (Figure 4B,E–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by cryo-EM structural data shown in Figures 4B, E-G.

claim: Trp193 of HsTMEM120A forms a strong π-π stacking interaction with the adenine group of CoASH.
source: Trp193 of HsTMEM120A forms a strong π-π stacking interaction with the adenine group of CoASH.
evidence: This claim is supported by cryo-EM structural data showing the interaction in Figures 4F-G.

claim: Mutation of the Trp193 to Ala dramatically reduced the affinity between CoASH and the protein.
source: Mutation of the Trp193 to Ala dramatically reduced the affinity between CoASH and the protein (Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC data comparing wild-type and W193A mutant shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: In the CoASH-free structure, the IL5 loop between TM4 and TM5 switches from the outward position to an inward position, partially covering the entrance of the intracellular cavity of HsTMEM120A.
source: In the CoASH-free structure (Figure 5A and B), the IL5 loop between TM4 and TM5 switches from the outward position to an inward position, partially covering the entrance of the intracellular cavity of HsTMEM120A (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of cryo-EM structures shown in Figures 5C-D.

claim: The absence of CoASH creates a spacious vacant lumen in the intracellular cavity of HsTMEM120A protein, potentially allowing water and ions to enter through the cytoplasmic entrance.
source: The absence of CoASH creates a spacious vacant lumen in the intracellular cavity of HsTMEM120A protein, potentially allowing water and ions to enter through the cytoplasmic entrance (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by pore profile analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The cavity appears to be constricted at a narrow region on the extracellular side mainly by four amino acid residues, namely Met207, Trp210 and Phe219, and Cys310.
source: Meanwhile, the cavity appears to be constricted at a narrow region on the extracellular side mainly by four amino acid residues, namely Met207, Trp210 and Phe219, and Cys310 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by pore profile analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A-C.

claim: Only Trp210 is highly conserved across different species among the four residues at the constriction site.
source: Among them, only Trp210 is highly conserved across different species, while the other three are less conserved (Figure 4—figure supplements 2 and 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 4—figure supplements 2 and 3.

claim: In the presence of CoASH, the intracellular cavity of HsTMEM120A is not only constricted by the four residues at the extracellular side but also blocked by the bulky adenosine 3-phosphate 5-pyrophosphate group of CoASH as well as its cysteamine and pantothenate groups.
source: In the presence of CoASH, the intracellular cavity of HsTMEM120A is not only constricted by the four residues at the extracellular side but also blocked by the bulky adenosine 3-phosphate 5-pyrophosphate group of CoASH as well as its cysteamine and pantothenate groups (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by pore profile analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A-B.

claim: Piezo1-transfected P1-KO-HEK cells showed robust MA currents.
source: Using a piezo-driven blunted glass pipette to mechanically probe the cell membrane under a whole-cell recording configuration, we recorded robust MA currents from the P1-KO-HEK cells transfected with the construct of either Piezo1 or Piezo2 (Figure 1A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from whole-cell patch-clamp recordings shown in Figure 1A-C.

claim: Piezo2-transfected P1-KO-HEK cells showed robust MA currents.
source: Using a piezo-driven blunted glass pipette to mechanically probe the cell membrane under a whole-cell recording configuration, we recorded robust MA currents from the P1-KO-HEK cells transfected with the construct of either Piezo1 or Piezo2 (Figure 1A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from whole-cell patch-clamp recordings shown in Figure 1A-C.

claim: None of the cells transfected with MmTMEM120A-mCherry showed poking-induced currents.
source: By contrast, similarly to vector-transfected cells, none of the cells transfected with the construct of either mouse TMEM120A (MmTMEM120A, with or without C-terminal fusion of fluorescent protein; MmTMEM120A-mCherry, with mCherry fused to the C-terminal region of MmTMEM120A; MmTMEM120A-ires-GFP, MmTMEM120A and green fluorescent protein (GFP) were translated as two independent proteins not fused to each other, due to the presence of an internal ribosome entry site/ires) or HsTMEM120A-mCherry showed poking-induced currents (Figure 1A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from whole-cell patch-clamp recordings shown in Figure 1A-C.

claim: None of the cells transfected with MmTMEM120A-ires-GFP showed poking-induced currents.
source: By contrast, similarly to vector-transfected cells, none of the cells transfected with the construct of either mouse TMEM120A (MmTMEM120A, with or without C-terminal fusion of fluorescent protein; MmTMEM120A-mCherry, with mCherry fused to the C-terminal region of MmTMEM120A; MmTMEM120A-ires-GFP, MmTMEM120A and green fluorescent protein (GFP) were translated as two independent proteins not fused to each other, due to the presence of an internal ribosome entry site/ires) or HsTMEM120A-mCherry showed poking-induced currents (Figure 1A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from whole-cell patch-clamp recordings shown in Figure 1A-C.

claim: None of the cells transfected with HsTMEM120A-mCherry showed poking-induced currents.
source: By contrast, similarly to vector-transfected cells, none of the cells transfected with the construct of either mouse TMEM120A (MmTMEM120A, with or without C-terminal fusion of fluorescent protein; MmTMEM120A-mCherry, with mCherry fused to the C-terminal region of MmTMEM120A; MmTMEM120A-ires-GFP, MmTMEM120A and green fluorescent protein (GFP) were translated as two independent proteins not fused to each other, due to the presence of an internal ribosome entry site/ires) or HsTMEM120A-mCherry showed poking-induced currents (Figure 1A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from whole-cell patch-clamp recordings shown in Figure 1A-C.

claim: Piezo1 mediated robust stretch-induced currents under both cell-attached and inside-out recording configurations.
source: As a positive control, Piezo1 mediated robust stretch-induced currents under both cell-attached and inside-out recording configurations (Figure 1D–I).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from patch-clamp recordings shown in Figure 1D-I.

claim: HsTMEM63a serves as a high-threshold mechanosensitive channel.
source: Consistent with the previous report that human TMEM63a (HsTMEM63a) serves as a high-threshold mechanosensitive channel (Murthy et al., 2018), we indeed found that HsTMEM63a-transfected cells reliably showed slowly activated stretch-induced currents, despite the maximal current amplitude being smaller than that of Piezo1-mediated currents (20.4 ± 2.2 vs 64.1 ± 7.4 pA) (Figure 1D–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research and experimental data shown in Figure 1D-F.

claim: HsTMEM63a-transfected cells reliably showed slowly activated stretch-induced currents.
source: Consistent with the previous report that human TMEM63a (HsTMEM63a) serves as a high-threshold mechanosensitive channel (Murthy et al., 2018), we indeed found that HsTMEM63a-transfected cells reliably showed slowly activated stretch-induced currents, despite the maximal current amplitude being smaller than that of Piezo1-mediated currents (20.4 ± 2.2 vs 64.1 ± 7.4 pA) (Figure 1D–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from patch-clamp recordings shown in Figure 1D-F.

claim: The maximal current amplitude of HsTMEM63a-mediated currents was smaller than that of Piezo1-mediated currents (20.4 ± 2.2 vs 64.1 ± 7.4 pA).
source: Consistent with the previous report that human TMEM63a (HsTMEM63a) serves as a high-threshold mechanosensitive channel (Murthy et al., 2018), we indeed found that HsTMEM63a-transfected cells reliably showed slowly activated stretch-induced currents, despite the maximal current amplitude being smaller than that of Piezo1-mediated currents (20.4 ± 2.2 vs 64.1 ± 7.4 pA) (Figure 1D–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from patch-clamp recordings shown in Figure 1D-F.

claim: None of the MmTMEM120A- or HsTMEM120A-transfected cells (a total of 57 cells) showed stretch-induced currents under either cell-attached or inside-out patch configurations.
source: By contrast, under either cell-attached or inside-out patch configurations, none of the MmTMEM120A- or HsTMEM120A-transfected cells (a total of 57 cells) showed stretch-induced currents, similar to vector-transfected cells (Figure 1D–I).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from patch-clamp recordings shown in Figure 1D-I.

claim: The cryo-EM structure of HsTMEM120A-CoASH complex was resolved to 3.7 Å resolution.
source: The combined data resulted in a 3.7 Å density map from 410,963 particles after the entire process.

claim: The cryo-EM structure of HsTMEM120A in detergent was resolved to 4.0 Å resolution.
source: The final map was generated through a subsequent local refinement in cisTEM (Grant et al., 2018) (RRID:SCR_016502) and was reported at 4.0 Å resolution according to the gold standard Fourier shell correlation (GSFSC) criterion.
evidence: This claim is supported by cryo-EM data processing described in the Methods section.

claim: The overall channel activity of HsTMEM120A protein reconstituted in GUVs is fairly low.
source: Most other patches were either silent and insensitive to the negative pressure applied (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C) or exhibited leaky signals, suggesting that the overall channel activity of the protein reconstituted in GUVs is fairly low.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from single-channel recordings shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The HsTMEM120A-mCherry construct contained a natural variation of residue 201 (A201 instead of T201).
source: Compared to the amino acid sequence of HsTMEM120A reported by Beaulieu-Laroche et al., 2020, the HsTMEM120A-mCherry construct contained a natural variation of residue 201 (A201 instead of T201).
evidence: This claim is based on sequence comparison with the prior published sequence.

claim: Both HsTMEM120A (T201A variant)-mCherry and GFP-HsTMEM120A were tested for the function in mediating stretch-induced currents.
source: To exclude the possibility that this variation might affect mechanically activated channel activities of HsTMEM120A, we also synthesized the cDNA of HsTMEM120A (with codons optimized for expression in HEK293 cells) encoding the exact same amino acid sequence as that reported by Beaulieu-Laroche et al., 2020 and cloned it into the pcDNA3.1 vector with an upstream GFP-encoding sequence (GFP-HsTMEM120A). Both HsTMEM120A (T201A variant)-mCherry and GFP-HsTMEM120A were tested for the function in mediating stretch-induced currents.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental design described in the Methods section.

claim: The A260/A280 value of the protein was lowered to 0.58–0.62 after size-exclusion chromatography.
source: The A260/A280 value of the protein was lowered to 0.58–0.62 after size-exclusion chromatography.
evidence: This claim is supported by spectrophotometric measurements described in the Methods section.

claim: The endogenous CoASH in the protein sample can be removed by purifying the protein through the size-exclusion chromatography in a detergent solution.
source: The endogenous CoASH in the protein sample can be removed by purifying the protein through the size-exclusion chromatography in a detergent solution (see 'Materials and methods' for details), as indicated by the decrease of A260/A280 (absorbance at 260 nm/absorbance at 280 nm) value from 0.88 to 0.58 (note: while the protein absorption maximum is at ~280 nm, the absorption maximum of CoASH is at ~260 nm; Zarzycki et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by spectrophotometric measurements and citation to prior research on CoASH absorption.

claim: The drastic difference in the single-channel conductance measured in cells and reconstituted lipid membranes raises the concern whether TMEM120A itself might indeed form a bona fide ion-conducting channel.
source: The drastic difference in the single-channel conductance measured in cells and reconstituted lipid membranes raises the concern whether TMEM120A itself might indeed form a bona fide ion-conducting channel.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the discrepancy between prior published data and the authors' observations.

claim: The lack of TMEM120A-mediated currents is highly unlikely due to the influence of the fusion tags.
source: Given that none of the four different versions of TMEM120A constructs (MmTMEM120A-mCherry, MmTMEM120A-ires-GFP, HsTMEM120A-mCherry, and GFP-HsTMEM120A) exhibited poking- or stretch-induced currents in the cells, the lack of TMEM120A-mediated currents is highly unlikely due to the influence of the fusion tags.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on testing multiple construct variants.

claim: Both the N- and C-terminal regions of TMEM120A are suspended in cytosol and distant from the transmembrane domain.
source: In line with the observation, both the N- and C-terminal regions of TMEM120A are suspended in cytosol and distant from the transmembrane domain, so that the fusion tags at the N- or C-terminal region might cause only minimal or no influence on protein function.
evidence: This claim is supported by the cryo-EM structural data showing the topology of TMEM120A.

claim: The fusion tags at the N- or C-terminal region might cause only minimal or no influence on protein function.

claim: TMEM120A might only respond to certain forms of mechanical stimuli such as perturbation at the cell-substrate interface.
source: Nevertheless, we cannot completely rule out the possibility that TMEM120A might only respond to certain forms of mechanical stimuli such as perturbation at the cell-substrate interface, which might require further independent verification.
evidence: This claim is speculative, acknowledging a possibility that requires further investigation.

claim: In case that TMEM120A does function as a mechanosensitive channel, the CoASH molecule may serve as a plug to block the intracellular entry and consequently stabilize the channel in a closed state.
source: In case that TMEM120A does function as a mechanosensitive channel, the CoASH molecule may serve as a plug to block the intracellular entry and consequently stabilize the channel in a closed state, while the intracellular cavity may become accessible to ions upon dissociation of CoASH molecule from the cavity (Figure 5—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This claim is speculative, proposing a hypothetical mechanism based on structural observations.

claim: The intracellular cavity may become accessible to ions upon dissociation of CoASH molecule from the cavity.
source: In case that TMEM120A does function as a mechanosensitive channel, the CoASH molecule may serve as a plug to block the intracellular entry and consequently stabilize the channel in a closed state, while the intracellular cavity may become accessible to ions upon dissociation of CoASH molecule from the cavity (Figure 5—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This claim is speculative, proposing a hypothetical mechanism based on structural observations.

claim: When the channel is further activated by mechanical stimuli applied to the membrane, the constriction site on the extracellular side may open wider for ions to pass through the pore.
source: When the channel is further activated by mechanical stimuli applied to the membrane, the constriction site on the extracellular side may open wider for ions to pass through the pore.

claim: TMEM120 protein shares structural similarities with ELOVL protein.
source: Recently, it has been reported that TMEM120 protein shares structural similarities with a membrane-embedded enzyme named elongation of very long chain fatty acid (ELOVL) protein (Niu et al., 2021; Xue et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to recent structural studies.

claim: It is possible that TMEM120A may utilize different substrates or catalyze a reaction distinct from that of ELOVLs if it functions as an enzyme.
source: Although TMEM120A did not exhibit ELOVL-like enzymatic activity when malonyl-CoA and stearoyl-CoA were supplied as substrates (Niu et al., 2021), it is possible that TMEM120A may utilize different substrates or catalyze a reaction distinct from that of ELOVLs if it functions as an enzyme.
evidence: This claim is speculative, proposing alternative enzymatic functions for TMEM120A.
